blocks.content: Chandigarh is a small but exam-heavy Union Territory — its geography questions cluster around one central, unusual fact: it is the joint capital of two different states (Punjab and Haryana) while itself belonging to neither. Everything else in this chapter builds outward from that single administrative oddity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India is located in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres, bounded by the Himalayas in the north and the Indian Ocean in the south.
The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) divides India into almost two equal climatic zones.
The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30' E, determining Indian Standard Time (IST) which is GMT +5:30.
India has diverse natural features ranging from northern mountain chains to coastal plains and peninsular plateaus.
India shares international land borders with 7 neighboring countries.

blocks.content: Chandigarh lies in north-west India at the foothills of the Shivalik range of the outer Himalayas, in the fertile plains between the Sutlej and Yamuna rivers — a location deliberately chosen after Partition for a new, unencumbered capital.

The Union Territory is landlocked and entirely surrounded by two states: Punjab lies to its west and north, and Haryana lies to its east and south. This makes Chandigarh a small administrative island — one of the smallest UTs by area — wedged between the very two states it serves as capital for.

Because it borders only Punjab and Haryana and touches neither Himachal Pradesh nor any other state directly, Chandigarh is often set as a 'connecting-the-dots' geography question: name the only two states bordering the UT.

cells: ≈ 114 sq km — one of the smallest Union Territories by area
Punjab (west & north) and Haryana (east & south) — only these two
Foothills of the Shivalik Hills (outer Himalayas), Punjab plains
Sutlej (west) and Yamuna (east) form the wider inter-river plain in which the city sits; the seasonal Sukhna Choe stream runs through the city itself
Humid subtropical — hot summers, cold winters, monsoon rains
1 (Chandigarh district — the entire UT is a single district)
Originally 47 sectors were planned (numbered, not named) in Le Corbusier's grid; the city has since expanded with additional peripheral sectors and villages

rows: Continuous, crossed only through passes (Thal, Bhor, Pal Ghats)
Discontinuous and dissected by major eastward rivers

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Classic one-liner: 'Chandigarh is the ONLY Union Territory (and one of very few places in India) that serves as the capital of two different states — Punjab and Haryana — while being a separate UT itself.'

cells: Hot and dry; May–June temperatures can cross 40°C
South-West monsoon brings the bulk of annual rainfall
Cold, foggy mornings; occasional near-freezing nights; January is the coldest month

items: Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
The 82°30' E Standard Meridian passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
Indira Point (6°45' N) in Andaman & Nicobar is the southernmost point of India, while Kanyakumari is the southernmost tip of the mainland.
The Sukhna Choe — a seasonal hill stream flowing from the Shivaliks — was dammed in the 1950s to create Sukhna Lake, now the city's most iconic natural/artificial water body (see Chapter 8).

Chandigarh sits in a mildly undulating plain that rises gently towards the Shivalik foothills in the north-east, giving the city's northern sectors (like Sector 1, housing the Capitol Complex) a slightly elevated, hill-facing character.
The UT has very limited forest/hill terrain of its own but borders the biodiversity-rich Shivalik foothill belt, which shapes its planning around green wedges and the Leisure Valley.
Chandigarh: ≈114 sq km; borders only Punjab (west/north) and Haryana (east/south); 1 district for the whole UT.
It is the capital of BOTH Punjab and Haryana, despite being a separate UT belonging to neither.
Located at the foothills of the Shivalik Hills, between the Sutlej and Yamuna river plains.
Sukhna Choe (seasonal stream) was dammed to create Sukhna Lake.
Originally planned in 47 numbered sectors (not named) — a distinctive, exam-favourite planning fact.
